items.description: The Venice of Africa, a lake village unlike any other
items.longDescription: Ganvié is an exceptional lake village on Lake Nokoué. With 30,000 inhabitants living in stilt houses, it is the largest lake city in Africa. Life revolves entirely around the water: floating markets, schools, places of worship. Residents travel by pirogue in a fascinating daily ballet.

items.description: One of the last great wildlife sanctuaries in West Africa
items.longDescription: Pendjari National Park is a conservation jewel of West Africa. Spanning 275,000 hectares, it shelters exceptional wildlife: lions, elephants, buffalo, hippos, cheetahs and more than 300 bird species. The Tanougou waterfall and the Atacora mountains add to the beauty of the setting.

items.description: Spiritual heart of Vodun and memorial of the slave trade
items.longDescription: Ouidah is a city steeped in history. The Slave Route and the Door of No Return bear witness to the tragedy of the slave trade. The city is also the cradle of Vodun, with the Temple of Pythons and the Sacred Forest of Kpassè. Every year on 10 January, the National Vodun Festival draws thousands of pilgrims.

items.description: The royal palaces of Dahomey, a World Heritage site
items.longDescription: Abomey was the capital of the powerful Kingdom of Dahomey for nearly 300 years. The royal palaces, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site, are adorned with remarkable bas-reliefs that tell the story of the kingdom. The historical museum houses priceless treasures: thrones, weapons, ritual objects.

items.description: Fine sandy beaches, traditional fishing and a relaxed atmosphere
items.longDescription: Grand-Popo is a peaceful seaside resort where the Mono River meets the Atlantic Ocean. Its long coconut-palm-lined beaches invite relaxation. The fishing village preserves its traditions. The Bouche du Roy offers magnificent scenery.

items.description: The vibrant economic capital, between tradition and modernity
items.longDescription: Cotonou is the beating heart of Benin. This dynamic city blends modernity and tradition. The Dantokpa market, one of the largest in West Africa, is a total immersion in local life. Red Star Square, Notre-Dame Cathedral and Fidjrossè beach are all worth discovering.

items.description: Gateway to Somba country and its tatas
items.longDescription: Natitingou is the main town of Somba country, known for its unique traditional dwellings: the tatas. These miniature mud fortresses look like little castles. The region offers magnificent landscapes of hills and valleys.

items.description: The administrative capital, rich in history and traditions
items.longDescription: Porto-Novo, the capital of Benin, is a city with a rich historical heritage. The Honmè Museum (former royal palace), the Afro-Brazilian-style Great Mosque and the Garden of Plants and Nature are all sites worth discovering.
